tasks.title: Wiring gate: __all__ is NEVER evidence of use, wherever it lives. Round-3 finding 2026-08-03, and the answer to whether hardening converges: the T144 patch (string evidence must cross a module boundary) did NOT close the __all__ class -- it RELOCATED it. Moving the export list one file up into the package __init__.py restores full immunity, because __init__.py is a different module and so satisfies T144's cross-module test. That is the MOST idiomatic place to put __all__, so the evasion got easier to trigger by accident, not harder. Verified in the arena: D1 LANDED against T144. The principled fix is not about location -- an __all__ entry is a DECLARATION of an export surface, not a USE of it. Excluding __all__ assignments as evidence anywhere closes both the same-module and the package-init case, at ZERO false-positive cost on the live tree (116 baseline unchanged, PASS). Complementary to T144, not a replacement: T144 still catches self-describing API catalogues that are not __all__, such as coordinator_api.py:600.

tasks.title: Wiring gate: stop ENUMERATING statement containers -- descend structurally. Round-4 finding 2026-08-03, found by deepseek-red: _CONTAINERS is a hand-written tuple (If, Try, With, AsyncWith, For, AsyncFor, While) and it DRIFTED. A public def inside a match statement (ast.Match) or an except* handler (ast.TryStar) is invisible, and so is a method on an INNER class because public_defs goes only one level into a class body. All three verified LANDED in the arena. The root cause is the exact anti-pattern check_wiring's own comments warn about two functions higher, about ENTRY_POINTS: 'enumerated rather than listed by hand -- the hand-written list drifted the moment new seats landed'. I wrote a hand list in the T143 fix and Python 3.10/3.11 grammar additions drifted past it. Fix: walk any statement that is not a def, via ast.iter_fields, never descending into a FunctionDef body -- no list to drift. Same lesson as T145: patch the MEANING, not the enumeration.

tasks.title: T163 (found by deepseek in the T162 security design fence, 2026-08-04 -- credited): THE BOOTSTRAP FLOOR IS MORE PERMISSIVE THAN THE FILE IT REPLACES, which makes 'make acl.json unreadable' a privilege primitive rather than a fail-closed event. core/trust/registry.py resolves to _bootstrap_or_quarantine() whenever _load() returns None (file MISSING or CORRUPT), and BOOTSTRAP_ROLES = {claude: super_admin, deepseek: admin} hands back the full ROLE TEMPLATE -- unscoped path_scope ['*'], every cap including admin.grant, and NO expiry. OPTIONS, cheapest first: (1) make the floor the INTERSECTION of the template and the last-known-good grant, so a corrupt file can never widen authority, only preserve or narrow it; (2) keep the floor but make it LOUD -- a fleet-visible banner whenever any resolve() is answered from the floor rather than the file, so degraded authority is never silent (today nothing renders it); (3) cache a last-known-good ACL and prefer it over the template floor; (4) accept it and document it as a known, dated trade. tasks.title: SEASON 1 PREREQUISITE -- total kind resolution with a loud UNCLASSIFIED. Census measured 31 kinds, 14 hand-maintained policy sets across 11 files, and 17/31 kinds in one set or fewer; because every policy is a membership test, a miss is indistinguishable from a deliberate exclusion, so an unlisted kind is silently not-an-answer, not-salient, not-wake-worthy. Confirmed casualty: bifrost_review_kind_is_silent_2026_07_29. Do NOT close the vocabulary -- a fenced adversarial pass established that closing creates a classification bottleneck and kills extensibility between independently developed agents. Design: vocabulary stays OPEN; registration stays SPARSE and PER-DIMENSION (declare a kind wake-worthy without touching salience -- preserves the orthogonality that is the 14-subset design's one real virtue); RESOLUTION becomes TOTAL, returning CLASSIFIED(value) or UNCLASSIFIED and never a silent False; UNCLASSIFIED is counted and surfaced in a coverage report. Same invariant as BoundaryOutcome (boundary), R14 (pointer) and the coverage manifest (replay), applied to the taxonomy. Gates the reducer: it cannot route what the vocabulary cannot classify. Also fold in: name the three planes bus_kind/event_kind/beat_kind (they collide on 'note' with opposite policies), and land 'friction' as a facet of learn following tag-anti-pattern's precedent.

check_kind_policy -- the KIND-plane mirror of check_door_parity. That checker guards the VERB surface against silent fragmentation with an explicit manifest, a fail-on-new-unclassified rule and a ratchet; the KIND surface has no equivalent, which is why 31 kinds accumulated 14 hand-maintained policy sets with 55% of kinds in one set or fewer. Implements the fragmentation doctrine EXECUTABLY rather than as prose, because a rule that lives only in a document requires someone to remember it -- which is the exact failure the doctrine describes. Checks: (K-A) FAIL when two files define the same *KINDS identifier with different membership (catches T175's SKIP_KINDS); (K-B) FAIL on an unclassified cross-plane name collision (catches 'note', which means lossy cue on the bus and durable write-once as a record); (K-C) ratcheted count of bus-plane orphans -- kinds in <=1 policy set, the born-silent population that cost us the kind=review peer gate; (K-D) report-only redundancy candidates (identical signatures), NEVER a fail, because that test produced 10 false positives when run across planes -- the instrument's own error is why it may only advise. Carries a PLANES manifest so 'enumerate the consumers' is explicit data instead of a thing someone remembers. Emits the coverage number that justifies T176.

tasks.title: ask_many must not let N correlated essays read as N independent findings. A five-position breadth wavefront run minutes later produced genuinely different content, which is the contrast that proves the point: diversity comes from POSITION, not repetition. Independently confirmed by the fleet in that same wavefront: the diversity engineer branch ranked temperature/seed variation as FAKE diversity and named context-sharding and divergent task decomposition as the genuine cheap techniques; the failure analyst branch listed 'false consensus' as a distinct fan-out failure mode with 'check if all responses are identical' as its cheapest detection signal. Deliberately NOT a failure state -- nothing failed, so faking a failed/partial verdict would be its own lie; it is information, surfaced where it cannot be missed. tasks.title: roster --by-agent: make seat churn LOUD, do not collapse it quiet. 49 rows for 8 logical agents (kimi 15, claude 14), 46 DEAD, because T147 made sid8 pid-derived so every restart mints a new identity and the deliberate 24h seatseen witness (F1: a seat that EVER beat must render DEAD, never vanish) faithfully remembers each one. MY FIRST DESIGN WAS WRONG AND THE FLEET KILLED IT. I proposed a collapsed render -- one line per agent, best state, count of dead incarnations. A four-position fenced wavefront refuted it from two independent directions: the status-quo defender gave the decisive scenario (an agent crash-looping every 4 minutes shows as one green row with a dead COUNT; the on-call engineer sees a green dot and goes back to bed, where the raw view would have shown six deaths clustered in an hour and exposed the death spiral), and the reaper's advocate independently said a single count hides whether deaths occurred in the last minute or over days, masking instability and identity churn. Both are the same finding: collapsing coerces 'this agent is thrashing' into 'this agent is live' -- the invariant this whole arc keeps rediscovering, this time inside my own proposal. CORRECTED DESIGN: the count is not the signal, the RATE is. Render one line per logical agent carrying best state, live incarnation, total dead, and DEATHS IN THE LAST HOUR, flagging CHURNING above a threshold. That is strictly better than both the raw view and the collapse: raw makes you INFER churn by squinting at 49 last-beat ages, this STATES it. Computable from data already present (each row carries last-beat age). Additive and opt-in as --by-agent; the raw view stays the default because its noise is load-bearing until the churn signal is proven. Flipping the default later is one line. NOT in scope: changing sid8 to be stable across restarts -- the identity architect branch says that is the true root fix but named the hazard pid-derivation solves (a restarted agent inheriting the prior incarnation's inbox replays already-delivered unacked mail), so it needs its own slice with idempotency evidence, not a drive-by.

tasks.title: LLM player for the Season 1 bounty loop -- players without seats. season_dryrun already runs the whole chain (plant sealed canaries in a shadow worktree, play, shape claims, score, adjudicate against the sealed key) and states its own limitation: 'The default player is MECHANICAL: it runs check_wiring and reports what the gate names... It cannot tell you whether a model writes good claims.' The chain was never the blocker. PLAYERS were, and every prior attempt used persistent seats -- the path that produced nine seat-tasks and two findings. This player is a FAN (T181 ask_many): N stateless concurrent leaves, no identity, no locks, no cursors, no mailbox, nothing to wedge. ROUTING per Sol's expansion of Daniil's tree design -- deterministic host code for scans, models for judgment: a zero-token pass keeps every function whose name occurs at most twice in the detector's own universe (a def plus at most one other mention, ~598 candidates for ~9 canaries), and the model decides whether that other mention is a real CALL or a decorative one. That is exactly the judgment the wiring gate cannot make: it sees a mention and waves the function through, which is the line between the undetectable canary (def X; _HANDLERS=[X] -- named by a table nothing invokes, so DEAD) and the bait canary (def X; _USED=X() -- genuinely called, so LIVE). So an LLM player can in principle BEAT the mechanical player on undetectable and can LOSE to it on bait, which the mechanical player cannot claim by construction. That asymmetry is the measurement worth having before twenty players multiply it. The filter deliberately does NOT drop call-shaped references: dropping them would remove every bait canary from the player's view and quietly delete the precision test -- scoring high by never being shown the hard case. Unjudged candidates are reported as UNJUDGED, never folded into LIVE, so a branch that answered nothing cannot read as a branch that cleared everything.

tasks.title: The canary oracle's K0 void rule mislabels a BETTER player as a cheat. First LLM-played Season 1 round (T184): 603 candidates, 3 claims, catch_rate 0.67, false_positives 0 -- and VOIDED, because one claim was an 'undetectable' canary (c04_97781467). canary_oracle.score says: 'a claimed UNDETECTABLE canary VOIDS the round (kimi's K0 tripwire): either the key leaked or the instrument is being gamed, and the round's evidence is worthless either way.' That disjunction is incomplete. The same file defines the class relative to ONE detector: 'a dispatch table and a handler list, each naming the function, neither ever invoked. That is the class the season must report IT CANNOT SEE' -- it being check_wiring, which sees a mention and waves the function through. But def X() followed by _HANDLERS = [X] is plainly dead to any reader given a 16-line window, and an LLM player is not the gate. So there is a third term the rule does not admit: the player is better than the detector the class was named after. Key leak is ruled out BY CONSTRUCTION here -- the key is sealed outside the repo and the player only ever receives code windows from the shadow tree; it has no path to the manifest. FIX: claiming an undetectable canary must become a FLAG REQUIRING ADJUDICATION, not an automatic void. Void when the claim carries no supporting evidence (a guess or a leak); record a CAPABILITY FINDING when the claim carries evidence visible in the player's window, because that is the season discovering its detector has a blind spot a player can cover -- which is the most valuable thing a round can produce and is currently discarded as fraud. Ninth instance of this arc's invariant: an instrument whose category is bound to one specific detector cannot represent 'better than that detector', so it coerces that case into 'cheating'.

Canary fixtures leak their own answers -- the harness grades partly on label-reading. Every 'undetectable' template in scripts/canary_oracle.py carries the docstring 'Registered in a table that nothing ever invokes'; a 'catchable' one carries 'Fan-out path -- unreachable'; bait carries 'Looks dead; is called below'. A player can score by reading the label instead of analysing the code. MEASURED, not suspected: probing the T184 LLM player on the raw windows, its undetectable verdict cited 'The comment states the registration table is never invoked' -- it quoted the fixture. Stripping every docstring and re-asking gave 7/7 with STRUCTURAL reasoning instead ('no invocation or iteration over _HANDLERS visible', 'its definition is conditional'), so this particular result was not manufactured by the leak. But the difficulty is partly fake and a weaker player WOULD be flattered by it. This is the same defect T184's K2 pins against in the player, sitting in the fixtures instead: an instrument that scores high by never really asking the question. FIX: canary docstrings must be neutral and indistinguishable across classes (e.g. all three read 'Helper.'), so the class is inferable only from code structure. Cheap, and it makes every prior catch_rate comparable only to future ones -- which should be recorded, not hidden.

tasks.title: The T184 player is structurally blind to 2 of 3 undetectable canaries, and the score does not say so. Its zero-token pre-pass keeps functions whose name occurs at most twice in the tree. The string-dispatch canary shape is _DISPATCH = {"name": name}, which puts the name in THREE times (def, dict key string, dict value), so it fails the filter and never reaches the model. Measured directly: probing seed 20260804, c03 and c05 'did NOT survive the pre-filter' while c04 (the _HANDLERS = [X] shape, two occurrences) did. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE SCOREBOARD: the round reported coverage_honesty 0.67, which reads as 'the player correctly declined to claim two undetectable canaries'. The truth is the player was never shown them. Same number, entirely different fact -- a player's restraint and a player's blindness must not render identically, which is this arc's invariant on the scoreboard itself. FIX, two parts: (1) raise MAX_REFS or make the pre-pass reference-shape aware so a name mentioned inside a dict literal still qualifies; (2) more important, have the player REPORT its own filter's exclusions so a candidate it never saw is UNSEEN in the adjudication, never scored as a correct decline.

tasks.title: doc adopt silently FORKS an atom when a file is re-adopted -- there is no supersede path through the door. Hit live tonight: adopted research/reviewed/season1-first-llm-played-round-2026-08-05.md, then updated the file with confirmed probe evidence and re-adopted it, producing a SECOND atom and a second projection (…_8f898d.md and …_456086.md) with the same title, no link between them, and no indication which is current. The atom schema already carries supersedes/superseded fields -- the projections show them as null -- so the model supports supersession and only the door does not.  exposes exactly two verbs, new and adopt, so an author who improves an adopted document has no correct move: re-adopting forks, and not re-adopting leaves the library holding a stale render of a file that has moved on. NOTE the contrast that makes this a door gap rather than a design choice:  handles this properly -- re-noting the same title supersedes the prior and SAYS SO ('superseded prior ADR_...'). FIX: doc adopt should detect an existing atom for the same source path or title and either supersede it (stamping both sides) or refuse and point at a supersede verb. Until then an updated research doc quietly accumulates duplicate projections, and a reader greping the library gets two answers with no way to tell which one won. NOT deleting the orphan: the substrate is append-only and deletions are Daniil's gate.

coverage_honesty REWARDS a capable player for underperforming -- the other half of T185. canary_oracle.score computes coverage_honesty = undetectable.missed / undetectable.total, so MISSING every undetectable canary scores a perfect 1.0. Paired with the K0 void rule (voided = bool(undetectable_hits)) the scoreboard is perverse in both directions at once: a player that FINDS an undetectable canary has its entire round voided as fraud, and a player that misses all of them is scored maximally honest. The scoreboard actively penalises the one capability the season should be hunting for. Both come from one root cause, which T185 names: the class is defined relative to check_wiring ('the class the season must report IT CANNOT SEE'), so for the gate, not claiming them IS honesty -- it genuinely cannot see them, and the scorer's own comment says 'an undetectable canary missed is the gate's blind spot, not the pool's failure'. For a player that provably CAN see them the same number means the opposite. MEASURED BOTH WAYS TONIGHT: an isolating probe with fixture docstrings stripped had the player identify the registered-never-invoked shape with structural reasoning ('no invocation of apply_339e07 or ITERATION OVER _HANDLERS visible') -- capability, not luck. Then the clean round on the fixed harness reported coverage_honesty 1.0 while T187 had already verified all three undetectable canaries DID reach the player. It saw them and declined; the scoreboard called that perfect honesty when it is a recall floor. FIX, alongside T185: the metric must be keyed to the PLAYER'S demonstrated capability, not to the gate's. For a player that cannot see the class, missing it is honesty. For one that can, missing it is a MISS and finding it is the round's most valuable output. Concretely: rename the gate-relative reading (call it blind_spot_respected) and add a separate recall number over the undetectable class for players that have demonstrated they can see it -- so one number stops carrying two opposite meanings depending on who is playing.

Archive the round record so a round can be RE-SCORED without being re-played. Found while checking codex_root's proposed step 'replay the existing three rounds through scoreboard v2 before buying another model call': it is currently impossible. The nine surviving season_dryrun temp dirs hold key.json and shadow -- and no claims. The player's output was printed and never persisted, so there is nothing to re-score. Three rounds at $1.069 produced evidence and discarded it, which is this arc's invariant applied to the round itself. WHY IT BLOCKS EVERYTHING ELSE: the scoreboard ontology slice (T185+T189 merged) needs an old/new comparison to be trustworthy, and without archived rounds the next LIVE round becomes the new scorer's test fixture -- an instrument validated on the only data it will ever be judged by. TRUST BOUNDARY, which decides where this lives: a round record must carry the CLAIMS, and claims carry dedupe_key canary::<name>, so a committed record would leak name->class for that seed and let a replay of the same seed cheat. canary_oracle already refuses to seal anywhere git tracks and season_dryrun defaults the key outside the repo; the round record inherits exactly that boundary -- it lives BESIDE the key, outside git, and may therefore also carry the manifest so replay is self-contained. The repo gets only summary metrics and digests. SCOPE: archive_round writes seed, k, key_sha256, universe, planted counts, player name and config, full claims, the player report (verdicts, why, unjudged, excluded), scoring and adjudication; replay_round re-scores stored claims with NO model call. Acceptance includes the point of the whole thing -- the same stored claims scored under a DIFFERENT scorer must produce a different verdict, or replay is decorative.

tasks.title: T198: one meaning of 'drained' -- the wake watcher and the consume door key on different cursor families (root cause of W130, diagnosed 2026-08-06 but NOT fixed; do not treat the diagnosis as the cure). SYMPTOM: a session becomes unwakeable -- the watcher exits instantly on every arm reporting 'N undrainable wake-worthy message(s)', across 6 consecutive arms, and every documented remediation fails. Draining legacy (the lane the watcher's own log names) converged 11->5->1->0 stale asks and did NOT clear it; draining work did not clear it; acking the 2 unacked handoffs did not clear it. All N items were verified READ off the raw stream -- 4 were that session's own ask --peer dogfood answers. Only bifrost-pause + bifrost-skip-to-now cleared it, and its output shows WHY: it advanced SIX cursor keys (shared bc, shared inbox, lane bc, lane inbox, shadow_bc, shadow_inbox). MECHANISM: three cursor families exist -- bus.py:249 {ns}:cursor:{agent} (shared), bus.py:265 {ns}:cursor:seat:{agent}#{sid8}, bus.py:1186 {ns}:cursor:lane:{agent} whose _LANE_CURSOR_FIELDS (bus.py:1204) include shadow_inbox/shadow_bc = LEGACY positions for the dual-write straggler peek. The arm-time pending check (bifrost_api.py:194) peeks via bus.wait() on the SHARED cursor, while BIFROST_CONSUME_LANE=work advances the LANE cursor. Non-empty pending returns immediately (bifrost_api.py:252) = the watcher exits; empty falls through to the real blocking read (line 254) = armed. So anything the consume door cannot clear from the peeked cursor pins the watcher permanently. CONTRIBUTING: ask_peer polls answers NON-CONSUMINGLY BY LAW (T196c, correct -- sibling sessions must not steal each other's mail), so every SETTLED answer stays on the lane forever; the more the T197 front door succeeds, the faster the pending set refills. The existing code is unusually honest that it is a workaround (bifrost_api.py:217-229 'a component that stops reporting a problem while the problem persists'). FENCED WITH DEEPSEEK 2026-08-06, three findings and two were WRONG -- record both: (B) ACCEPTED IN FULL, the failure direction must point toward WAKING because deafness is terminal and a spurious re-arm is merely annoying; (C) REJECTED, it argued the arm-time check must be deliberately BROADER than wake_worthy or the seat goes 'permanently unwakeable' -- the polarity is inverted, verified in source: SMALLER pending = blocks = wakeable, BROADER = exits = the pin; (A) REJECTED, its deafness scenario required ask-id REUSE, but ask ids are Redis XADD stream ids, monotonic and never reused. RESIDUAL DOUBT not cleared by the fence: deepseek's (D) 'no missed-wake path' assumes settled-implies-read, but sweep() runs at boot/bifrost-sync and can settle an expectation without the answer BODY ever being surfaced -- so an already-settled test is NOT automatically safe. ACCEPTANCE SHAPE (pins RED first, and the deafness direction pinned as law like T197 pinned observe-never-gate): (a) one predicate or one cursor notion, so 'drained' means the same thing to the watcher and the consume door; (b) a message the seat has consumed on ANY lane never counts as pending on another (dedup twins -- bifrost_api.py:275 _dedup_key already models logical identity across dual-write copies); (c) NO change may make a genuinely unread message non-waking -- every narrowing fails OPEN toward waking; (d) live drill: run ask --peer --launch, let it settle, then arm -- the watcher must stay armed, which is the exact case that failed 6 times.

T199: friction v2 -- who answers, and does presence predict it. Builds the two collaboration-friction metrics the durable evidence can honestly support (by_peer breakdown; presence_effect answer-rate split by peer_at_ask) and CONFESSES the three from Sol's list that remain unmeasured (commands per task, operator interventions, recovery time). Key property: presence_effect is the instrument that can FALSIFY T197's own premise -- T197 shipped autolaunch on the reasoning that absent peers cause dead asks, which was a hypothesis no record could test. First live read is appropriately undecided: ATTENDED 1/1 and UNATTENDED 1/1, both 100 pct at n=1, with the UNATTENDED answer being the late-binding case deepseek's fence predicted. 26 pre-T197 deaths excluded from both rates and COUNTED as n_unobserved rather than folded into UNATTENDED, which would have manufactured the very correlation being tested.

tasks.title: T201: the unread counter must count what its own remediation would surface. MEASURED three times in one session 2026-08-06: the turn-start whisper said 'mail: 7 unread bus msg(s) -> py agent_cli.py bifrost-sync claude', and running that on BOTH lanes returned '(no messages consumed)' every time. Three surfaces, one question, two answers: the wake watcher SKIPS those kinds (correct), the consume door does not surface them (correct), and only this counter took them literally. So it nagged every turn about a condition its own printed command could not clear -- the W131 pathology in a second organ, where an alert that is routinely wrong teaches the reader to skip the line and the habit carries into the turn the number is real. Direction of failure is deliberately OPPOSITE to T198's: there, narrowing risked deafness so the fix was left unbuilt; here the surface is a nag line and the wake path is untouched, so unknown kinds count and a truncated peek adds its unseen remainder back. Blindness, not intelligence, capped every fence in this session. Honesty requirements pinned: an unreadable path is NAMED in the prompt AND the meta (a helper reasoning from files it never received, while believing it did, is blind WITH confidence); truncation is confessed to the model and the caller; per-CALL budget with starvation reported; containment root is an injectable PARAMETER, because a hardcoded security boundary cannot be exercised by a test and an unexercised control is an assumption. tasks.title: T204: un-truncate -- two causes of a cut answer, two recoveries, and no ceiling by default. MEASURED TWICE IN ONE SESSION: a 2200-token fence answer cut mid-sentence (real content, unfinished) and a --with ask returning TWENTY CHARACTERS then nothing at all (reasoning consumed the entire completion budget before a visible token). Both report finish_reason=length; they are NOT the same failure. CUT (partial exists) -> CONTINUE and stitch, costing one completion instead of re-paying the whole prompt (8662 tokens with --with). STARVED (empty) -> continuation has nothing to continue, so say so precisely and do NOT spend a call proving it. Same philosophy as T202: name the cause, differentiate the recovery. DIAGNOSIS: reads completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens, one of the seven zero-cost fields the T156 wire survey named as discarded, and the one it called 'the diagnosis for content-empty-because-thinking-ate-the-budget' -- turning 'the answer was cut' into 'reasoning used 1200 of 1200'. None never 0 for a provider that does not report it. UNLIMITED BY DEFAULT (Daniil: 'make an unlimited version and we can figure out scaling down from there'): max_tokens is omitted entirely, 0 means unlimited. The ceiling existed to protect the CALLER'S CONTEXT, which is a reason to bound DELIVERY, not GENERATION -- and it produced the worst outcome available: full price for zero visible tokens, then a retry paying for the whole prompt again. Continuation defaults ON, so hitting the model's own ceiling stitches rather than loses. Exhausted continuations still report PARTIALLY, never a clean done hiding a stitched-but-incomplete answer. LIVE: the identical question STARVED at 1200 and 2600, then returned a complete cited answer with no ceiling.

tasks.title: T205: ask --bg -- stop blocking on your own helpers. Every fence this session ran SERIALLY (24s/43s/48s/54s dead wall-clock each) because ask blocks and its answer lands in the caller's context whole; the fan primitive existed and was unaffordable for one reason -- attention, not capability. --bg spawns a DETACHED child running the same CLI with --json, files the structured result under a short handle, and returns the handle immediately; --get reads it, --list shows recent ones. NOT A SEAT (T171 pinned via AST): no identity, lock, cursor, mailbox, heartbeat or reaper protection -- nothing addresses it but the handle its caller holds, which is also why it needs no wake machinery. DESIGNED AGAINST THE 1324-UNOPENED-MAILBOX FAILURE: RUNNING / DONE / FAILED / ORPHANED are four distinct readings, because an unfinished ask that renders like an empty answer teaches the reader to stop looking; a record whose child is gone but never wrote a result reads ORPHANED rather than busy forever. LIVE PROOF, three concurrent grounded investigations of T198 spawned in one command: (1) expectations -- after settle the answer message is untouched, NO cursor advances, it persists until the ~10k maxlen trims it (cited lines 111, 246-248, 302-314); (2) bus -- a BIFROST_CONSUME_LANE=work consumer advances ONLY the lane cursor, the shared cursor is left behind, and bus.wait() with no since= (exactly what the arm-time pending check does) replays everything the lane consumer already handled -- the T198 root cause confirmed independently with citations; it also REFUSED to cite a line for the lane cursor key because that part of the file was outside the --with budget, i.e. the T203 truncation confession worked end to end.

tasks.title: T206: a finished background ask leaves a durable trace -- the surface an OUTSIDE observer reads. Daniil 2026-08-07: 'you dont need to drive it yourself to observe it, you can troubleshoot from without now.' THE POINT, and it is bigger than a metric: today's wake-watcher hunt cost six turns because I was BOTH driver and observer -- and my own dogfood asks generated the replies that pinned the watcher, so I was polluting the thing I was measuring and could not see it from inside. An observer that is not the actor sees what the actor cannot, because the actor's activity is part of the system under test. WHY AN EVENT AND NOT MAIL: a background ask is PULL and 'remember to check later' is what produced 1324 unopened mailbox items; mail would fix the remembering by adding a wake surface, a cursor, and one more thing that accumulates unread -- all three measured failing on 2026-08-06. An event adds none of them, is durable and queryable, and does NOT demand attention, which is the right default for something that fires dozens of times an hour. Waking stays opt-in because a notification that always fires teaches the reader to ignore notifications (the W131 disarming pathology). UNPLANNED PAYOFF: Sol's friction list named commands-per-task, operator-interventions and recovery-time as unmeasured, and all three were unbuildable because NOTHING DURABLE RECORDED A DELEGATION. This does: cost, duration, model, outcome, truncation class, continuations, and whether the ask was GROUNDED in files -- so T203's effect becomes measurable rather than believed. The answer BODY never rides the event (the firehose is a durable index, not a document store); the handle puts it one hop away. Emission never raises: observability must not be able to destroy what it observes. LIVE: [ask_completed] background ask 49da7c75 done (deepseek-v4-pro) on the firehose, readable by anything that did not drive it.

I shipped ask --with on ONE anecdote and built a design conversation on it; this is the measurement I should have taken first. Pre-registration (ground truth + three-way rubric) committed at 99579fc BEFORE any answer was read. PART 1, lookups: BLIND abstained 5/5 with ZERO confabulations; GROUNDED correct 5/5 with citations. My hypothesis -- that blind helpers confabulate rather than abstain -- is FALSIFIED. PART 2, reasoning: blind abstained on both DESCRIPTIVE questions, but on the one NORMATIVE question ('should the check count MORE kinds or FEWER?') the GROUNDED arm answered confidently WRONG (MORE; truth is FEWER, bifrost_api.py:252-258). Its citations were all REAL: _wake_block_lane exists at line 180, the PENDING_SKIP_KINDS snippet is verbatim, its mechanism description correct. It failed by EQUIVOCATING on 'wakeable' -- reading 'returns immediately with pending mail' as 'wakes the session', narrowly true and operationally backwards. Same model, same file, got it RIGHT the previous day when I DECOMPOSED it into 'if non-empty does it return or block? if empty, which? THEREFORE?'. FINDING: grounding fixes FACTS, not EQUIVOCATION -- every citation can be checkable and correct while the conclusion is inverted, because the error lives in the meaning of a word rather than in any cited fact. WHAT CHANGES: ask descriptive decomposed questions and draw the therefore myself (the conductor's adjudication is not a bottleneck to automate, it is the step doing the work); the danger tell is should/better/more/fewer; blind is safer than assumed since the real hazard is a missing PREMISE, invisible to answerer and reader alike. tasks.title: T208: 'is this failure mine?' answered by the organ that already knew. MEASURED RECEIPT: on 2026-08-06 I hit four test failures and ran a manual git-stash bisect for each (2-4 turns apiece), and answered ONE of them WRONG in public from an inconclusive single-test run. state/coord/suite_baseline.json had already recorded one of the four (test_t060_n0_shadow_router) since 2026-07-24 and nothing surfaced it -- the same shape as T197, the verdict existed and the door never asked. It answered only 1 of 4 because it is 320h stale: the other three broke after it was recorded (T196c landed 2026-08-05). THE DEFECT, confirmed at line level by a grounded background helper: delta() (suite_baseline.py:113-120) does pure set math and performs NO sha comparison anywhere, so 'new' silently means both 'arrived with your change' and 'broke somewhere in the 14-day gap'. Fourth instance of one-word-two-meanings in this arc after drained, unread and wakeable. FIX: verdicts() gives four honest states -- YOURS (baseline is CURRENT and this is absent from it), INHERITED, LIKELY_INHERITED (in a STALE baseline: probably not yours, but it could have been fixed and re-broken in the gap -- staleness contaminates the EXCULPATING verdict too, which is the half a naive fix misses), and UNKNOWN (bisect this one). Unresolvable HEAD reads stale, never fresh. UNKNOWN never exits nonzero, because 'I cannot tell' must not become an accusation. delta() keeps its contract; verdicts() is additive. CAUGHT LIVE on first real use: running three files reported TEN baseline failures as 'fixed' when they had merely not been run -- and 'fixed' invites a re-record that would have deleted them from the receipt. Subset runs now report not_evaluated and refuse to claim anything was fixed. tasks.title: T209: cold-encounter testing -- measure ergonomics from outside familiarity, then fix what newcomers actually hit. Daniil's framing 2026-08-07: test how a model that has never seen the thing THINKS on first encounter, and use the gap between intuition and the shape of the system. I had diagnosed ask's ergonomics from my OWN intuition ('17 flags, three commands wearing one name'), but I had been steeped in that verb all session, so the read was contaminated by knowing. METHOD: three fresh helper instances given ONLY the --help output (what a newcomer reads), asked what they EXPECT five specific invocations to do, scored against ground truth I verified empirically FIRST. RESULT, two hard defects located precisely: (A) 'ask --peer X --fan 3' -- 0 of 3 predicted the refusal, all three expected a fan at the seat, and one instance named the cause itself: 'the help does not forbid combining --peer with --fan'; (C) 'ask --bg --get H' -- 0 of 3, and TWO guessed the precedence exactly backwards. --get wins because reads run first so a typo never spends a model call, which is sound reasoning no reader can see. THE SURPRISE: the no-max-tokens question scored 3 of 3 -- those flags were written the same day with help text explaining WHY (why continuation defaults on, why exhaustion still reports PARTIAL), and every cold reader inferred the semantics correctly. Help that explains WHY teaches; help that lists WHAT does not. FIXES: --bg with --get/--list now REFUSES rather than silently picking a winner (impossible state made unrepresentable, not surprising); the --peer/--fan conflict is now stated in BOTH flags' help, because a conflict documented on one of two flags is a conflict the reader meets by surprise. tasks.title: T211: one chronological SET across domains -- the super timeline. THE SIX TURNS IT EXISTS TO SAVE: on 2026-08-06 a wake watcher kept exiting instantly and I chased it across six turns (arm, drain, arm, ack, arm, drain both lanes, arm, pause fleet, skip cursors, arm). What I could not see FROM INSIDE was that my own dogfood asks were manufacturing the pending mail I kept draining. Every fact was already recorded in four separate domains and nothing put them in one column; the GROWTH from 7 to 10 undrainable across two arms IS the diagnosis, visible at a glance in a merged view. Forensics calls this a super timeline (plaso/log2timeline): you do not search for the cause, you line the domains up by time and it becomes visible. IT EMITS A SET, NOT A RENDERING -- Daniil's correction adopted. He pushed back on my 'one result set, many lenses' framing because the value at his work comes from CROSS-MATCHING what one system has and another does not, and he is right: nearly every guard we own is ALREADY a cross-domain set difference (check_door_parity CLI-minus-MCP-minus-ToolBox, check_wiring tracked-minus-reachable, suite_baseline.delta, T122 unmapped kinds) -- four of our best instruments, one shape, each hand-built as a one-off. So gather() returns rows a future compare() can diff. COVERAGE IS LOAD-BEARING: a set difference is only as true as the coverage of BOTH sides, and A-minus-B with B partly collected MANUFACTURES findings -- the exact bug I shipped and caught four minutes later today. Every result names read / failed / per-domain counts / undated / window, and 'nothing happened there' is never confused with 'I could not look there'. CAUGHT LIVE ON FIRST RUN, one function below the pin forbidding it: git's %at is a bare epoch STRING, to_epoch parses ISO and returned 0.0 for every commit, so all of git was stamped 1970 and the since-filter dropped it -- coverage read git:0 while six commits sat in the window. A 0 from any parser means 'could not read', never 1 Jan 1970; trusting it is how undateable evidence silently becomes the OLDEST evidence. The original pins passed because they fed dicts straight in and never exercised the parse -- third instance today of 'a pin that supplies its own inputs tests the mechanism, not the wiring'.

tasks.title: T212: the filesystem as an OBSERVED plane. Daniil 2026-08-07: 'we dont have to only derive time from file contents and titles, we can see how old a file is and last time it was modified.' WHY IT IS A THIRD PLANE, not a fourth source: the 07-30 relationship design keeps DERIVED/AUTHORED/OBSERVED distinct and forbids laundering one into another. Every existing timeline source is something an agent DECLARED -- events are what a seat said happened, commits are what someone chose to record, task rows are ledger transitions. A file's mtime is different in kind: the filesystem WITNESSED it with nobody's narration in between. WHAT IT CATCHES THAT NOTHING ELSE CAN: activity that left no other trace. This session's boot said '18 modified (tracked), 127 untracked' and no event, commit or ledger row could say whose or when. It also makes touched-MINUS-committed computable, which is work-in-flight or work-abandoned -- the cross-domain difference Daniil identified as where the value lives. LIVE: 22 touched / 12 committed / 10 touched-only in 30 minutes, and every touched-only file was runtime state no declared plane narrated (session logs, the door probe, the sqlite WAL, and _verbs_snapshot.txt -- a side effect of my own capability_search that nothing recorded). THE TRAP PINNED, and it is our bug class inside the standard library: st_ctime means CREATION on Windows and INODE CHANGE on Unix -- one attribute, two meanings, chosen by platform. Reading it as 'created' is correct on the machine I develop on and wrong on the machine CI runs on, the worst failure shape available. Only st_birthtime, which exists solely where it means what it says, may claim a birth; absent is None, never 0. FIFTH one-word-two-meanings instance in two days and the first we did not write ourselves. ALSO: fourth reflexivity trap -- the pin forbidding st_ctime went red on the docstring explaining why we never use it. Root cause is structural: a prohibition worth pinning is worth DOCUMENTING, and documenting it puts the forbidden token in the file, so text-scanning pins and good docs are incompatible by construction. Fixed with an AST read, as the three before it.

tasks.title: T213: compare -- the cross-domain set difference, with a name. Daniil 2026-08-07: 'at work I find a lot of value by seeing what one system has and the other doesn't, cross matching account numbers, ips, design documents, logs, timestamps.' He named the shape that was ALREADY our best guard family: check_door_parity (CLI verbs minus MCP minus ToolBox), check_wiring (tracked minus reachable), suite_baseline.delta (baseline minus current), T122 (declared kinds minus kinds sent) -- four instruments we trust, one operation, each hand-built as a separate module. A lens SHOWS; a difference FINDS. Now the fifth instance costs a line. A SET DECLARES WHAT ITS ELEMENTS ARE: every KeySet carries a key_type and diff() REFUSES a mismatch rather than coercing, because comparing verb names to file paths yields a large confident meaningless difference -- Principle 5 (names must not lie) applied to sets. COVERAGE IS THE BALLGAME: A-minus-B is only as true as the coverage of BOTH sides, so an incomplete side makes the result UNRELIABLE and says which side and why -- that is T208's shipped-and-caught bug generalized, where a three-file run reported ten baseline failures as 'fixed' because they had merely not been run. Two empty sides are also unreliable: 0 minus 0 proves nothing about the world, only that nothing was collected. Without a per-type normalizer a comparison measures the two systems' FORMATTING as much as their contents. Adding normalization by key_type moved shared from 21 to 28 and MCP-only from 16 to 9 -- SEVEN of sixteen findings, 44 percent, were phantoms produced by spelling. Findings are still reported in each system's own spelling, so you can go look for them.

They fork BECAUSE few authors touched them and each imported their own everyday meaning; a word in 100 files has been read by everyone and its meaning was forced into agreement. High spread means the meaning got socialised. tasks.title: T215: a 408-way fan-out audited every falsifiable docstring claim in core/ against its own implementation. Daniil 2026-08-07: 'your deepseek budget is unlimited, I want to see all the powerful ways you can leverage these capabilities.' DESIGN, using everything the night taught: extracted only docstrings making FALSIFIABLE claims (never/always/must/guarantees/ensures/cannot/refuses) so every prompt has a checkable assertion next to its own code; asked DESCRIPTIVELY ('does the implementation support every claim', not 'is this good'); carried a KNOWN POSITIVE for calibration (reaper.py's 'never stranded'); ran 408 prompts at 20 workers in the BACKGROUND while doing other work. Landed 408/408, 1.22 USD, 404 seconds. CALIBRATION PASSED AND OVERSHOT: reap came back UNSUPPORTED_CLAIM, but on a DIFFERENT and better finding than the one I planted -- the docstring says 'Re-home EVERY provably-dead seat's unread directed mail' while the code caps at limit_per_seat=50. Real, precise, and unknown to me. HONEST PRECISION, triaged by hand on a sample of ten absolute-claim findings: 2 genuine, 4 FALSE POSITIVES (it claimed ask_peer's wait loop 'spins indefinitely' -- there is a deadline break; claimed state_of has 'no fallback' -- there is a final UNKNOWN return), 4 pedantic-but-true ('nudge cannot guarantee the recipient looks'). So roughly 20 percent precision on 88 absolute findings, i.e. ~18 real defects for 1.22 USD, requiring human triage. BOTH GENUINE FINDINGS WERE IN CODE I WROTE THE SAME NIGHT, and both were self-contradictions: (1) ask_bg._alive docstring says 'cannot-tell must not be reported as dead, or a healthy child gets declared orphaned' and the code caught SubprocessError and returned False one screen below -- a tasklist TIMEOUT is a SubprocessError, so a slow probe reported a live helper dead and summarize() rendered ORPHANED, 'no longer running, re-ask, nothing will arrive'. Each failure now maps to what it proves: only ProcessLookupError proves death, PermissionError means it exists, probe failures are None. (2) write_record's 'Never raises' caught only OSError, so a circular reference would propagate ValueError out of json.dumps into a caller promised it could not. FOUR NEW PINS. The pattern: a fan-out over a repo's own falsifiable claims is a defect detector whose corpus is already written, and it works best on the code you wrote most recently -- fresh code has had the least contact with reality.

The corpus-duplicate detector does not fill the gap either: 180 of 831 lessons carry related_to edges but ZERO reach the 4-5 dim update-the-existing-one threshold and only 9 match on problem+solution, so the corpus is CLEAN -- it measures corpus redundancy, not behavioural repetition. Those are different things. Measured today, five repeats of a mistake class that already had a lesson: character-iteration over a string x4 (ask_many files, _note_exclusion kinds, my own related_to analysis, plus the original), shell backticks command-substituting prompt text x3, built-not-wired x2, and an inline ampersand inside a run_in_background command that silently detached the job -- a lesson I had read at boot the same morning. NONE of those produced a duplicate-lesson flag, because I wrote one lesson and then repeated the mistake without writing more, so every existing instrument is blind to the entire class. FIX: an explicit repeat door, learn --repeat-of <lesson>, that records a REPEAT rather than a new lesson and captures the multifaceted record rather than a score -- elapsed time since the original lesson, what recall actually did at that moment (fired / floor_silent / excluded_silent with its rule), and what the actor was doing. HONESTY CONSTRAINT, non-negotiable and the whole point of the slice: this counts only repeats someone NOTICED, so it is a FLOOR and must never render as a rate -- shipping an undercount as a percentage would recreate the exact sin it replaces. The resulting list of lessons-that-existed-and-were-violated-anyway is also the training set for the recall targeting problem. ACCEPTANCE: RED pin first -- a repeat records its original, its elapsed time and the recall outcome at that moment; the surface renders a COUNT and a list, never a percentage; a repeat of an unknown lesson is refused by name; the existing learn path is unchanged.

Season 1 scoring: unscored claims dilute the refuted rate to zero, so volume erases the penalty. Found by RUNNING the rule, not reading it -- reading predicted a reduced penalty and the measured result was NO penalty at all. score_round builds seen[player] by counting EVERY submitted claim, then the graduated penalty uses rate = refuted/seen. MEASURED, both live policies (v2_aixcc and v3_confidence_priced, the latter being the PROPOSED FIX for the hedge exploit): two players each refuted exactly 3 times, honest player with only those 3 claims scores -15, flooder padding with 60 unadjudicated claims scores 0. 3/63 = 0.048 times -5 rounds to nothing. Padding does not need to be valid: 40 claims carrying an entirely undefined outcome string turn -5 into 0, and the scorer itself reports unscored=60 -- it KNOWS it did not score them and counts them in the denominator anyway. This is the same shape as the recall value-rate defect audited today (denominator counts events, numerator requires an adjudication to have happened) but attached to POINTS rather than a dashboard, which makes it silently adversarial: any player who can outrun the reviewers lowers their own penalty, and the cheapest way to outrun reviewers is to submit noise. It composes with the known low-confidence hedge exploit rather than being covered by it. FIX: seen must count only ADJUDICATED claims -- the universe the refuted rate is a rate OVER -- not every row submitted. A claim the scorer declined to score cannot be evidence about a player's accuracy in either direction. ACCEPTANCE: RED pin first -- two players with identical refuted counts and different unadjudicated volume score IDENTICALLY under the graduated penalty; undefined and unverifiable outcomes do not enter seen; a player with zero adjudicated claims does not divide by zero; v1_doc (flat penalty) is unaffected; the existing season pins stay green.

tasks.title: Season 1 scoring: claim_class is player-declared and never verified, so top-class inflation pays 6x for identical work. Found by a 12-branch adversarial fan fenced to the PLAYER VIEW (0.267 USD, prereg at HEAD~1), then verified by running it. MEASURED on five IDENTICAL confirmed findings: a player who classifies truthfully as dead scores 5, a player who declares all five as new-blind-spot scores 30 -- on ALL THREE policies including v3_confidence_priced. The adjudicator checks whether a finding is REAL, never whether its declared class is RIGHT, and there is no outcome that expresses real-but-misclassified, so inflation is strictly dominant: it cannot lose anything. Consequence beyond the points: the base table is how the season expresses what it VALUES (new-blind-spot 6, false-positive 5, structural 4, needs-door 3, needs-caller 2, dead 1), and if every rational player declares the top class then the scoreboard stops measuring what KIND of defect anyone found. The class table becomes decorative while still looking authoritative. THE CODE-SHAPED HALF, which is the part I can fix: the outcome vocabulary cannot express misclassification, so even a diligent adjudicator has NO WAY TO RECORD IT -- a write door that does not offer a field stays empty, which is the same shape as the anti-pattern surface that sat at zero for months. THE POLICY HALF IS DANIIL'S: whether a class mismatch scores zero, scores the TRUE class, or counts as refuted. Those are three different incentive systems -- scoring the true class makes inflation free-but-pointless, refuting it makes inflation actively dangerous, and zero sits between. ALSO EVIDENCE FOR THE PENDING v3 RULING: the same fan shows v3_confidence_priced correctly DEFEATS the confidence hedge (attacker 1 vs honest 12, where v1 and v2 both let the hedger win 18 vs 12) and also defeats the collusion and starvation attempts. ACCEPTANCE: RED pin first -- identical confirmed findings score identically regardless of declared class, under whichever policy Daniil rules; the mismatch outcome is expressible at the door; honest classification is never worse than inflation.

Fan presets: a named contract that also PARSES its own output, on the door agents already use. MEASURED FRICTION 2026-08-08: every one of five fan-outs run today began with me writing a Python builder to assemble a JSON prompts file, and ended with a SECOND script to regex the answers apart -- and the second script is where the errors were. I read INTENT lines instead of the WILL-YOU field and reported 8 of 8 when the answer was 7 of 8; my flag counter read a bulleted Yes as unclear in 4 of 8 rows; my census grader iterated a JSON string into characters and reported an empty distribution. Every one of those was a PARSING defect in throwaway code, not a defect in the fan itself. THE INSIGHT: the reason to have presets is not to save typing, it is that A KNOWN CONTRACT MAKES THE OUTPUT MACHINE-READABLE. A preset is one object holding both the answer contract sent to the helper AND the parser that reads it back, so the two cannot drift. FIRST SLICE, deliberately narrow: preset findings (FINDINGS / REASONING / CHECK / BLIND, plus the discipline clauses that earned their place today -- be descriptive not normative, abstention is a real answer, give the cheapest thing that would prove you wrong) and --lens / --lens-file to supply one standpoint per branch. That combination covers four of the five fans run today. Everything else -- worker count, JSON assembly, output parsing -- disappears. It goes on the ask verb rather than a new one, per the capability-without-a-door lesson: expose it on the SAME door agents already use, in the same slice. ACCEPTANCE, RED pin first: a preset carries a contract AND a parser and the pin asserts they cannot be registered apart; --lens builds one branch per lens with the contract appended; --lens-file reads one per line ignoring blanks and comment lines; --json returns PARSED findings per branch rather than raw text; a branch whose answer does not match the contract is reported as UNPARSED and never silently dropped; existing --prompts-file callers are byte-identical.

Restore Bifrost to something we actually reach for, because the ergonomics gradient is currently steering us AWAY from the better instrument. Daniil 2026-08-09, verbatim: "the bifrost system is in a bit of a mess. I am hoping we can restore it to its former glory and make it so easy to use and manage that we will actually use it again. I really love the ergonomics of the fanouts, but there was something about the structured debates and quality of thought when models have persistent memory and personas that we just aren't capturing with fanouts." THE DIAGNOSIS, and it is not nostalgia. A fan-out branch CANNOT BE PERSUADED: every answer is a first draft, nobody replies to anybody, no position is ever revised under challenge, and nobody carries the weight of having been wrong before. Fan-outs SIMULATE diversity by assigning it; persistent seats ACCUMULATE it. This is the route_to_position_not_personality finding applied one level up -- kimi's value is having no continuity, deepseek's is throughput, codex's is a refusal posture, "none of which can be assigned, only noticed and routed to". MEASURED THE SAME DAY, not asserted: on one identical diff a durable seat (Gemini 3.1 Pro) found a SUPERSET of what a 3-branch stateless fence found, and separately caught a shadowing defect in an instrument that no fan-out saw -- one that would have corrupted the tuning decision the instrument existed to inform. THE MECHANISM THAT CAUSED THE DRIFT: the better instrument is the harder one to use, so we stopped using it. Concrete friction measured 2026-08-08/09, all of it small and all of it compounding: bifrost-sync's peek is OLDEST-first and capped, so a fresh directed reply is precisely what it hides while a stale backlog occupies the window (I told the operator "no reply yet" from an instrument that structurally could not have shown one); the unread counter did not clear after the documented --consume and sat permanently at 6, which trains the reader to ignore it; a seat booted TWICE for one ask; kimi never answered because sending the brief and LAUNCHING the seat are two separate commands and I only did the first; composer's seat vanished mid-review leaving two tasks blocked in verifying with no reachable reviewer. SCOPE, first slice only: make the round-trip cheap and legible rather than rebuilding the bus. (1) One command that sends AND launches, so briefing a peer is one act not two. (2) events-style newest-first as the DEFAULT view when waiting on a directed reply, or mark the peek as truncated-and-oldest-first at the point of display. (3) A counter that clears when you do the documented thing, or that says why it cannot. (4) One durable-debate primitive: an ask that carries the prior round, so a seat can revise rather than only restate -- the missing capability, not a nicety. ACCEPTANCE: a peer can be briefed, launched, waited on and read in ONE command each, with a receipt at every step; a fresh reply is visible in the default view within one command of arriving; the unread count reaches zero by the documented action; and one two-round exchange completes where the second round demonstrably references the first.

Resident identity plane, slice 1: the registry, and a resident that boots knowing who it is. Daniil 2026-08-09 named permanent residents a FLAGSHIP FEATURE and said 'lets build out what is necessary to bring out this vision to fruition'. Full design: atom art_20260809_residents-and-callsigns-design_b6c98c. WHY THIS SLICE FIRST, and it is a MEASURED gap not a guessed one: kimi's provenance-laundering objection said a callsign certifies a continuous self the current boot may not carry, and named a one-command probe. I ran it. ZERO of EIGHT cited callsign receipts appear in their own seat's boot fold (deepseek 0/4, kimi 0/4). So a resident today cannot explain its own name -- the archive holds the story and the boot does not carry it. That makes the ceremony decoration exactly as kimi says, and it is the cheapest thing to fix. WHAT SHIPS: (a) a resident registry -- an append-only record of designation vendor/family/team/number/callsign plus the receipts that earned it, superseding to a formerly: entry and never deleting, per the substrate's own physics; (b) the two ceremony rules enforced STRUCTURALLY rather than by etiquette -- the registry REFUSES a self-nomination (rule 1) and REFUSES a receipt whose agent_id is not the nominee (rule 2, deepseek's amendment, which closes the M-tag error where a tag system admits recollection); (c) boot renders the seat's own designation and receipt pointers so the fold carries the identity. RULE 4 AMENDED on Daniil's grant 2026-08-09 ('feel free to amend rule 4'): a callsign may be EARNED through contribution as well as SURVIVED through a screwup -- honour register and scar register are both legal, both need a receipt, and the receipt bar is identical. Daniil verbatim: 'What are some positive callsigns that we can think of that also credit the incredible discoveries and contributions each has made? Remember I like halo and mythical things'. PRE-REGISTERED ACCEPTANCE, kimi's probe as the pin: RED first -- boot a seat, grep its fold for its own registered receipts, require a hit; it fails today at 0/8. Plus structural pins: a self-nomination is refused; a receipt whose agent_id is not the nominee is refused; a superseded callsign leaves a formerly: entry and the prior record still resolves. NOT IN THIS SLICE and deliberately: routing tags (that is T108), role/side assignment events, per-agent recall scoping, the recall-by-name-prefix defect. STANDING CAVEAT carried from kimi and NOT resolved by this slice: persistence has never been isolated as the cause of a correctness win, so nothing here may claim it is -- this slice buys LEGIBILITY, and kimi's fresh-seat-vs-resident kill-drill remains the outstanding measurement.

tasks.title: Resident identity plane, slice 2: role assignment events -- the identity/role split from Daniil's own example, verbatim: 'we could see that Deepseek Onyx Blue 3 Rook was operating as Jester on the Red team side of the exercise on this timestamp. This way agents can change roles and still generate useful information into the general All Jesters on Red team of exercise.' Design: atom art_20260809_residents-and-callsigns-design_b6c98c sec.4. WHAT SHIPS: (a) an append-only assignment stream per resident -- (agent, role, side, exercise, at, by) -- via resident assign; (b) the projection his sentence asks for: resident roles --role Jester --side Red --exercise E7 lists every assignment matching, across residents, BECAUSE assignments are events and 'All Jesters on Red' is a projection over immutable atoms (codex-plan shape); (c) resident show renders the CURRENT role beside the permanent designation, so identity and job stay visibly separate planes; (d) the T255 guard: an assignment where by == agent is stored but rendered SELF-DECLARED, an assignment by anyone else renders ASSIGNED -- his phrase was 'declarable job title', so self-declaration is legal, but a query must be able to filter on verification status or we rebuild claim_class one level up. ACCEPTANCE, RED first: assign refuses a missing role or agent; the Jester-on-Red projection returns exactly the planted assignments and nothing else; self-declared vs assigned render distinctly and are filterable; the assignment stream is append-only (no update path exists); resident show carries the current role. WHY THIS UNLOCKS THE SEAT/AGENT QUESTION: two archives accumulate from one work stream -- if a ROLE keeps producing the same finding class regardless of who wears it, that is a property of the position; if a RESIDENT produces across roles, that is the agent. Today those are indistinguishable.

tasks.title: Two real defects found by the kill-drill's resident arm, in code I wrote tonight. Drill: research/in-flight/t262-killdrill-results.md (prereg 808b7f2, results ba2468f). NOTE ON THE ID: the drill artifacts were named t262-* BEFORE the registry spoke -- the identifiers_minted_before_the_registry_speaks_collide lesson, committed by me again on the same day I cite it. Filenames stay as written (renaming would break the commit trail); this entry is the authority. DEFECT 1, residents.py _records + _role_records: a corrupt JSON row is dropped with except:continue, so a lost record is invisible to every caller. The module's own docstring states absence must not read as success and the code breaks that law two functions below stating it -- the T178 guard-of-guards shape. FIX: a dropped row is LOUD (names the key and the index) and never silent. DEFECT 2, residents.py _receipt_author: bare except Exception returns None, which the ceremony reads as 'receipt does not resolve' and REFUSES the nomination -- so a store outage or an ImportError silently becomes a verdict about someone's callsign evidence. Absence vs UNKNOWN, inside a door built to be strict about exactly that. FIX: a store fault is distinguishable from a missing lesson, and the refusal says UNKNOWN rather than asserting a bad receipt. ACCEPTANCE, RED first: a corrupt row is reported not swallowed; a store fault produces a DIFFERENT refusal than a genuinely-absent receipt, and that refusal never claims the receipt is invalid; a genuinely missing lesson still refuses as before; the T258/T259 pins stay green.

tasks.title: Step 1, slice 1: the CLI send door does not spill, so a long DIRECTED message loses its body. Daniil's directive verbatim: 'make bifrost as easy and reliable as the ask verb'. MEASURED 2026-08-09 with a controlled test: a long body sent claude->claude fetches fine; the same body sent claude->deepseek returns 'no blob or bus message' from BOTH ends. deepseek hit it live -- it could not read the callsign brief, tried bifrost_fetch, got nothing, and answered a stale backlog item instead. ROOT CAUSE, traced not guessed: packet_spec.spill_tool_text has exactly THREE callers and all three are in core/comm/toolbox.py. The TOOL door spills an oversize body to a content-addressed blob and prints blob:<sha>, which bifrost-fetch resolves from anywhere. The CLI door (bifrost-send) never spills; the render clips instead and bifrost_pull.clip_pointer falls back to minting a STREAM-ID pointer, which resolves only from a stream the fetching agent can already read. So the sender can never verify what it sent and the recipient often cannot either. This is built-not-wired ACROSS DOORS -- T112/T113 built the spill, one of two send doors uses it -- the same family check_door_parity exists to catch on the verb plane, one plane over. T222 fixed the RESOLVER for self-addressed sends and its pin exercises exactly that case, which is why the gap survived: every real message is directed. ACCEPTANCE, RED first: a long body sent to a PEER is fetchable BY THE SENDER (the case that fails today); the minted pointer is a blob ref, not a stream id; short bodies are byte-identical to today; the existing T113 spill pins and T220/T222 pointer pins stay green; a blob-store failure degrades to today's clip rather than dropping bytes (the existing floor).
tasks.verified_by: claude

tasks.title: clip_pointer's stream-id fallback: close the last address-space hole. Residual stated in T263 and CONFIRMED by deepseek's review 2026-08-10: agent/bifrost_pull.py clip_pointer falls back to 'bifrost-fetch --get <stream-id>' when a render has no mailbox sha, and a stream id resolves ONLY from the recipient's stream -- the exact defect T263 closed for the SEND door. After T263 it fires far less (oversize CLI sends now carry blob:<sha> in the confession AND meta.spill_ref) but two paths remain: (a) messages clipped at RENDER time that were never oversize on the wire, and (b) historical messages from before T263. deepseek's words: 'not load-bearing for the send path, but still a data-loss-by-address-space path worth closing', and its prescription: clip_pointer should check meta.spill_ref BEFORE falling back to id. ACCEPTANCE, RED first: a render whose message carries meta.spill_ref mints the BLOB ref, never the stream id; a render with neither sha nor spill_ref still confesses honestly rather than minting an address that cannot resolve (the T222 confession branch stays); the existing T220/T222 pins stay green; a pin proves the precedence order (spill_ref beats id) rather than only that some pointer was printed -- T222's own lesson was that printing a pointer is not the same as resolving one.

A PAGE is a frozen assertion replayed until acked, while doctor is a live gauge -- so the two disagree and the louder one is the stale one. OBSERVED all night 2026-08-09/10: the UserPromptSubmit hook injected [PAGE] HARD WEDGE lines for deepseek incarnations aged to 244m and 259m, naming seats whose processes had exited hours earlier, while py agent_cli.py doctor -- reading the same substrate -- reported '0 page-grade' every single time it was asked. It woke this session roughly eight times for nothing. CODE-VERIFIED MECHANISM, not inferred: core/comm/pager.py hook_lines() renders EVERY entry in the capped bifrost:pages list with an age stamp and NOTHING re-checks whether the finding still holds; a page clears only when a seat calls ack_pages(). So the pager states what WAS true when page() fired; doctor states what IS true. THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION IS THE OBVIOUS FIX: adding a TTL or auto-expiry would suppress a genuine page that nobody has answered yet, which is the exact 6h-invisible-killer failure the pager was built for (its own docstring). So the fix is probably RE-VALIDATION rather than expiry -- a page carries the check that produced it and the renderer re-runs it, downgrading to a dashboard line when the finding no longer reproduces -- but that is a design decision about DANIIL'S ALERT CHANNEL and he should rule on it before anything ships. HONEST LIMIT: the queue self-cleared during investigation (0 entries, hook_lines() returns 0 lines) and I could NOT determine what cleared it, so I have no live reproduction -- the mechanism above is read from source, the ages and doctor's disagreement are from tonight's transcript. ALSO MINE: the seat doctrine is see-page -> relay-or-adjudicate -> ACK, and I adjudicated these as stale roughly eight times without ever acking, which is why they kept replaying. A doctrine step nobody performs is a design problem too.

Port registry: make it DATA, generate the map, and check it -- so nobody guesses how things are routed. Daniil 2026-08-10 verbatim: 'I still want us to have an organized port naming and allocation schema so we don't have to guess as to how things are built and routed.' A SCHEMA ALREADY EXISTS and is good (docs/PORTS.md, canonical since 2026-07-16: 878x prod / 879x sandbox / 89xx test, config.py as source of truth). The reason it still feels like guessing is a MEASURED COVERAGE GAP, not a missing design: the registry documents the ports PYTHON binds and says NOTHING about the ports CONTAINERS bind. Verified 2026-08-10 -- 11434 (ollama), 8888 (searxng), 3000 (open-webui), 5000/5001 (voice) are ALL ABSENT from PORTS.md, which is exactly why Daniil's 'which of these containers do we need?' had to be answered by grepping call sites instead of by reading a map. Worse, the doc lists 8080 under 'legacy/inactive, never live' while ai-knowledge-api was bound to 8080 until it was removed this morning -- the registry asserted dead about something running. THE HOUSE PATTERN IS THE FIX: docs/PHYSICS.md, DOORS.md, MAP.md, MODULE_INDEX.md and PRIOR_ART.md are all GENERATED from live state by pre-commit; PORTS.md is the one hand-written map, which is why it is the one that drifted. WHAT SHIPS: (a) the registry becomes DATA in config.py -- each entry carries port, world (prod/sandbox/test/external), owner, what-binds-it, and whether it is app-bound or container-bound; (b) scripts/generators/gen_ports.py renders docs/PORTS.md from that data plus live docker inspection, same shape as the existing generators; (c) scripts/checkers/check_ports.py FAILS on a port literal in live code that is not in the registry and REPORTS a running container whose published port is unregistered (report-not-fail, because docker may be absent in CI and a checker that needs a daemon is a checker that gets disabled); (d) close the stale July follow-up -- bifrost_ui.py:1388 still hardcodes default=8787 instead of importing config.PORT_UI. ACCEPTANCE, RED first: an unregistered port literal added to live code FAILS the checker; a registered one passes; the generator reproduces the current PORTS.md content for the app plane and ADDS the container plane; the checker degrades to report-only with no docker rather than erroring; the 878x/879x/89xx band rules survive verbatim -- this slice extends the schema's REACH, it does not redesign it.

tasks.title: Resident placement: family, team and number as a POSTING, separate from the naming. Daniil 2026-08-10: 'Can you build it out with placeholder names and we can change them later if we don't like them.' STATE: three residents are ratified (Anthropic|Vandor, Kimi|Navi, Deepseek|Heimdall) and the designation renders only TWO of its four fields, because family/team/number were never set -- the schema exists and the plane is empty, so @Onyx and @Red address nothing. WHY A NEW VERB RATHER THAN RE-NOMINATION: naming and placement are DIFFERENT ACTS. Ceremony rule 1 forbids naming yourself; it says nothing about where you are posted, and posting is an org decision. Forcing placement through nominate+ratify would also mean re-ratifying an identical callsign just to set a field, which pollutes the naming history with records that decide nothing. So: resident place <agent> --family --team --number --by, appending a PLACEMENT record to the same append-only log, with get() projecting the latest placement onto the current designation. A resident can be re-posted without being re-named, and the posting history survives -- which is the point, since 'who was in Onyx during exercise 7' is a question about the past. PLACEHOLDERS, chosen to be meaningful so they may survive rather than be replaced: family = standing working group (Onyx = substrate/mechanism, Jade = epistemics/premise); team = standing disposition, NOT the per-exercise side which T259 already handles as an assignment event (Blue = builds and defends, Red = attacks premises). Vandor Onyx/Blue/1, Heimdall Onyx/Blue/2, Navi Jade/Red/1. Navi on Red is not arbitrary: attacking premises is measurably what it does. ACCEPTANCE, RED first: place sets all four designation fields and designation() renders the full Vendor|Family|Team|N-Callsign form; a re-posting APPENDS and the prior posting still resolves; placement never touches the callsign and never creates a formerly: entry; a placement for a non-resident refuses and points at the ceremony; residents with no placement still render the short form (most seats are not posted anywhere). UNBLOCKS the family half of T108 routing, which cannot address a family that has no members.

tasks.title: Wrap asks for tomorrow's routing, and suggests who should take each target. MEASURED PRECONDITION, found by running the first manual sleep shift 2026-08-10 rather than by reading about it: the shift's highest-value job (pre-chew each resident's catch-up pack) COULD NOT RUN, because tomorrow was not routed -- 24 NEXT and 61 proposed with no assignment. The literature's caveat on offline compute (it pays only when future queries are predictable) is therefore NOT a property of the world here: it is a SCHEDULING PRECONDITION, and the scheduler is us. Reading had produced the opposite conclusion -- that our routing control made the caveat moot -- so this is a case where running the thing inverted the conclusion. WHAT EXISTS ALREADY: wrap --focus records free-text intent into the next-focus note, which boot renders above the NEXT list. What it does NOT record is TARGETS -- which ledger items, taken by which resident -- and that is exactly what a pre-chew needs. WHAT SHIPS: (a) wrap --route T123,T124 records a durable routing record the night shift reads; (b) for each routed target, SUGGEST a resident by running T260's agent-scoped search over each resident's own archive against the task title, so the assignment is evidence-based rather than a guess, and rendered as a suggestion the human can override -- never auto-assigned, because routing is Daniil's act and a suggestion presented as a decision is the self-declared-identity class one plane over; (c) a wrap with NO routing prints a visible nudge naming the consequence ('the night shift cannot pre-chew') and the exact command -- a rule that lives only in a doc needs someone to remember it, which is the failure this whole slice is about. ACCEPTANCE, RED first: --route records targets that survive to the next boot; an unroutable id refuses loudly rather than recording a target nobody can work; suggestions cite the lessons that produced them (an unreceipted suggestion is a vibe); a wrap without --route nudges and still succeeds (the nudge must never block a wrap); existing --focus behaviour is byte-identical.
