tasks.title: WISHLIST id allocator races on stale reads, and 14 ids are already ambiguous. Surfaced live 2026-08-10 when filing W141: the door itself warns that W00 and W57-W69 each appear more than once. NOT a new discovery -- agent_cli.py:1940-1948 documents it from a 2026-08-01 measurement (128 blocks, highest W114, 14 doubled) -- but it has sat unfixed while every wish filed since inherits an ambiguous namespace. TWO HALVES, and only one is safe to do unattended. ROOT CAUSE (the half that matters): the allocator is n = max(existing) + 1 computed from a plain read, which never collides against a CORRECT read but always can against a STALE one -- two seats filing batches against different versions of the file. This is the same class as the store's lost-update hole and the answer is the same shape: allocate under a cross-process lock, or CAS the file, so the read that computes the id and the write that uses it cannot be separated. The door is right to file anyway on a collision (Daniil's standing rule is that capture must never refuse -- 'append the moment friction is felt'), so the fix belongs in ALLOCATION, never in refusal. DATA REPAIR (the half that needs a human): renumbering the 14 duplicates makes citation unambiguous but BREAKS every existing citation of those ids, and the corpus cites wishes by number at gates. That is a semi-destructive rewrite of a durable record and it is Daniil's call whether old citations should resolve to the first or second holder. Proposed: repair AFTER the allocator lands, so the renumbering happens once rather than racing new collisions in behind it. ACCEPTANCE, RED first: two concurrent wish filings never receive the same id (the pin drives real concurrency, not a mocked sequence -- a pin that supplies its own ordering tests the mechanism and not the wiring); a stale-read filing is detected and retried rather than silently colliding; the capture door still NEVER refuses a wish on a collision; the existing 14 duplicates are reported by a checker until repaired, so the debt stays visible rather than becoming furniture. BLOCKED TODAY on the agent_cli.py file lock held by T268.

T088 RECONCILIATION: the identity arc was specified 24 days before I re-derived it, and its FOUNDATION is still unbuilt. Found during the 2026-08-10 stale triage, not by search -- T088 'Agent identity and naming arc' (Daniel directive 2026-07-16) sat PROPOSED and untouched while I designed and shipped T258-T267 from Daniil's 2026-08-09 directive without ever reading it. WHAT MY WORK ACTUALLY DELIVERED, mapped honestly against T088's two halves rather than claimed wholesale: T088(b) DISPLAY-NAME LAYER -- LARGELY DONE. The callsign IS a display name split from the stable agent_id (ids stayed stable throughout; nothing addresses by callsign yet, which is the point of T108). T088 asked for an 'alias record formerly X' and T258 built formerly: independently -- convergent design, which is luck rather than method, and worth recording as such. T088(b) ID-MIGRATION RITUAL -- NOT DONE. A true rename must migrate cursors, claims and grants and emit a ledger event; supersede a callsign today and none of that moves, because a callsign is a label over an unchanged id. That is fine while ids never change and becomes a live defect the first time one does. T088(a) COLLISION-SAFETY -- NOT DONE AT ALL, and this is the foundation everything above sits on: there is no identity REGISTRATION handshake, so two agents spawning simultaneously with one id still conflate memory attribution, funnel credit, presence and cursors. The roster already shows the symptom -- multiple DEAD incarnations per agent, and seat_identity_is_process_scoped_not_session_scoped is the lesson filed about it. WHAT THIS SLICE IS: build T088(a), the registration handshake -- first boot CLAIMS the id or takes a suffix, with the claim durable and the conflict LOUD. Not the migration ritual (own slice, and only urgent once ids move). ACCEPTANCE, RED first: two processes racing to claim one id -- driven concurrently, never a mocked sequence -- produce exactly one holder and one suffixed seat, and the loser is TOLD which it is rather than silently continuing as a twin; an existing live holder is never displaced by a newcomer; the claim survives a crash without stranding the id (a lease, not a lock held forever). DO NOT close T088 on this: it carries three parts and this slice is one.

One clipper, not five: make CLIP -> CONFESS -> RESOLVE a chokepoint instead of an audit. Daniil 2026-08-10: 'How can we fix all clipping instances everywhere so we stop running into that issue?' WHY AN AUDIT CANNOT WORK, and this is the load-bearing reason: I tried twice to build a detector inline and both instruments over-counted badly (179 then 364 'silent truncations', mostly LIST slices like hits[:25] and receipts[:2] caught alongside genuine text cuts like body[:500]). x[:200] is not a clip -- it is a clip only when x is text someone else needs and will not see the rest of. Syntactically identical, semantically opposite. That is T214's wall exactly: token-level tools cannot detect forked MEANINGS, and 'a clip' is a meaning. So the fix must be a CHOKEPOINT that makes the next silent clip impossible to add, not a sweep that finds today's. MEASURED SURFACE: FIVE independent _clip implementations (core/events/event_log.py, core/primitives/distiller.py, agent/bifrost_pull.py, agent/harness/context.py, agent_cli.py) plus the packet_spec family (bound_tool_text / spill_tool_text / clip_stamp) and clip_pointer. One concept, five mechanisms, deliberately different tokens -- the forked-semantics class the LEXICON work exists for -- and only packet_spec's spill PRESERVES THE BYTES. The other four destroy. THE CONTRACT, paid for three times separately and never written down together: T220 clipped with no address (data loss by design); T222 minted an address that did not resolve and found that is WORSE, because a dead pointer looks actionable and costs a turn to discover it is decoration; T263 had the tool door spilling while the CLI door clipped. So: above a byte threshold SPILL to a content-addressed blob and return a ref that resolves from anywhere; below it DECLARE N-of-M and name a recovery command that actually runs; never a bare ellipsis. WHAT SHIPS: (a) one canonical clipper carrying the contract, with the four destroying implementations migrated onto it; (b) a ratcheted checker that fails a NEW raw text truncation outside the helper, freezing today's instances as a backlog exactly like check_wiring's 116 -- so 'where do we clip' becomes 'who calls the clipper', which is mechanically answerable; (c) clip_pointer taught to prefer meta.spill_ref before falling back to a stream id, which ABSORBS T264. ACCEPTANCE, RED first: a new raw truncation of a text variable in live code FAILS the checker; a clip above the threshold produces a ref that RESOLVES from a third party, not just from sender or recipient; a clip below it renders N-of-M plus a working recovery command, and the pin RUNS that command rather than asserting it was printed (T222's own lesson: verifying that a pointer was printed is not verifying that it resolves); the existing T113/T220/T222/T263 pins stay green. THRESHOLD IS MEASURED, NOT GUESSED: a 220-char inbox preview must not mint a blob, so the cut point is chosen from the live distribution of clip sizes and the choice is recorded. SEQUENCING: lands AFTER the n=5 drill reports -- it rewrites files the drill is currently measuring. Supersedes T264, which is the same defect seen through one door.

Kill-drill at n=5: does a resident's own memory cause findings a blind seat misses? Pre-registration committed at 947d238 BEFORE any answer existed. NOTE ON THE FILENAME, recorded rather than tidied: the prereg was written as research/in-flight/t273-killdrill-n5-preregistration.md before the registry spoke, and T273 was subsequently minted for the CLIP CHOKEPOINT slice. The file keeps its name (renaming breaks the commit trail at 947d238); THIS entry is the drill's real id, and the two are not related. Third time this week I have pre-named an artifact -- the identifiers_minted_before_the_registry_speaks_collide lesson, cited by me two days ago and violated since. THE QUESTION: kimi's verdict that persistence was never isolated as the cause of any win is unresolved, and five slices now sit on it. The n=1 run gave a favourable direction (resident 2 real defects, blind 0, foreign-memory 0) and FAILED both attribution bars because no finding named a lesson, so it could not tell recall from coincidence. THE CHANGE THAT MATTERS: the citation requirement moved INTO the brief and became machine-checkable -- each branch is asked which recalled lesson produced each finding, NONE explicitly legitimate and unpenalised, and the claim is verified against the pack actually sent. A cited id present in the pack is GROUNDED (bar 1); an id that was never in the pack is FABRICATED and scored separately, predicted in advance as H5 because asking for citations creates the incentive to produce them. THREE ARMS over 5 targets: blind, resident-with-own-archive, and blind-with-a-FOREIGN-archive -- the last re-run because its n=1 result (foreign memory scored WORSE than none) was the only unpredicted finding and is already cited as a build constraint, so it deserves confirmation before it hardens into doctrine. Confounds REMOVED rather than controlled: one file per call under the 40K budget, since the n=1 run passed 78K and the evidence clipped. ACCEPTANCE: the pre-registered scoring stands as committed; if H3 holds (blind equals or beats resident) the result is published in kimi's own framing and the design atom drops every correctness claim.

report verb: a design SYSTEM as a door, so a visual report costs content instead of CSS. Daniil 2026-08-10: 'Is there a way to verbify it so that it is easier for you to make these?' -- after three artifact reports in two days (night retrospective, decision brief, T272 reconciliation). WHAT IS ACTUALLY REUSABLE, measured by writing it three times: the dual-theme token system (ground/surface/line/ink/muted plus SEMANTIC colours that carry meaning rather than decoration), the type pairing (mono eyebrows and data, sans headings, serif for standfirsts and quoted directives), and six layout primitives -- the aurora rule, stat tiles, a card with a two-path split showing what each direction costs, a timeline, a side-by-side versus block for a genuine disagreement, and a scannable table with tabular numerals. That is roughly 200 lines rewritten three times with drift each time. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT REUSABLE, and this is the design constraint rather than a caveat: the SHAPE. The three reports needed three different structures because they were three different documents, and Daniil's praise was for the fit. A template that emits a fixed document would flatten exactly what he is responding to, and the artifact-design guidance warns specifically against templated output. So the verb hands over the SYSTEM and never the document. WHAT SHIPS: (a) design/report-kit.css -- the tokens and primitives in ONE place, so an improvement to the palette propagates instead of forking into a fourth variant; (b) py agent_cli.py report new --title <t> --out <path>, mirroring , which emits an HTML scaffold with the kit INLINED (the artifact CSP blocks external stylesheets, so inlining is a requirement rather than a convenience) plus a commented crib of every primitive with its class names, so composing does not require remembering them; (c) the primitives carry their SEMANTICS in the comments -- a two-path card is for decisions with real costs on both sides, a versus block is for a genuine disagreement and not for a pro/con list -- because a primitive used off-purpose is how a design system becomes decoration. ACCEPTANCE, RED first: the emitted scaffold renders standalone with no external fetch; both themes are defined at token level and the data-theme override wins over prefers-color-scheme in BOTH directions; the kit lives in exactly one file and the scaffold inlines it at emit time rather than linking it; a scaffold with no content still renders valid HTML; the crib names every primitive the kit defines, checked mechanically so a new primitive cannot be added without documenting it.

tasks.title:
Standing practice: capture the state of the art daily, synthesize weekly, and turn the gap into questions. Daniil 2026-08-10 after the Max call: "He said we need to daily be on the bleeding edge of tools and AI research to keep up with the industry. I want us to make that be a standard practice and I remember having a conversation about this very thing, we have yet to make it a reality."

CHECKED BEFORE DESIGNING, per i_designed_an_arc_the_ledger_had_already_specified: no prior ledger task covers a research CADENCE. What exists is ad-hoc: the 2026-08-09 handoff/repriming prior-art sweep and the 2026-08-07 ensemble scan. Both were one-offs triggered by a question. T229 fans across LEARNERS and is a different thing. So this is genuinely new, and Daniil's memory is right -- we have done the work twice and never made it an organ.

WHY IT IS NOW URGENT rather than nice: ████████████ (Meta, Ads ████████████; ████████████) reports having seen ELEVEN external memory schemas and about FIVE internal ones, all with different tradeoffs. We had researched benchmarks and five packages. That gap is the difference between knowing the field and knowing of it. He also offered to answer well-formed questions WEEKLY in a shared doc -- which makes a weekly synthesis self-justifying, because its output IS the question list.

WHAT SHIPS: (a) a daily CAPTURE door -- one command that files a source (paper, release, post, repo) into the store with a verdict field, so capture costs seconds and nothing lives in a chat scroll; capture is deliberately cheap and unopinionated, because a ritual with friction does not survive contact with a busy day. (b) a WEEKLY SYNTHESIS that renders four sections and nothing else: what is new, what we could FOLD IN, where we STAND versus the named competition, and the OPEN QUESTIONS the week produced. (c) the questions section feeds Max's doc directly, so the practice pays for itself in one hop rather than accumulating into a reading list nobody reads. (d) the report is a visual artifact via the T275 report verb.

THE HARD PART, and it is not the plumbing: RELEVANCE. A daily scan that files everything is a second inbox, and the corpus already carries a measured 4.8% value rate that says we are bad at predicting what will matter. So each capture must record WHY IT MIGHT MATTER TO US in one line at capture time -- the same discipline as a lesson's trigger clause -- and the weekly synthesis must report how many captures were actually folded in. A practice that cannot show its own yield is the funnel problem one level up.

DEPENDS ON, and this is a real dependency rather than a nicety: T277 (define what success looks like). Without a success definition, "where we stand versus the competition" has no axis and the comparison degrades to a feature checklist. Max's exact words: "if we don't define what success looks like we won't be able to measure progress towards it."

ACCEPTANCE, RED first: capture is ONE command and survives a body containing shell metacharacters (the W143 class); a capture without a why-it-matters line is REFUSED, because an unlabelled capture is a bookmark; the weekly synthesis renders all four sections from stored captures and never from a model's memory of the week; the synthesis reports its own fold-in rate; a week with zero captures renders "zero" rather than an empty page, so a lapsed practice is visible rather than silent.

Define what success looks like, so progress becomes measurable. ████████████, 2026-08-10, and it is the sharpest external critique this project has received: "if we don't define what success looks like we won't be able to measure progress towards it." He has seen eleven external memory schemas and about five internal ones and says they all trade off differently -- which is the same point restated: without a stated objective there is no basis for choosing a tradeoff, and every design decision becomes taste.

THE GAP IS REAL AND SPECIFIC, and it is not a gap in instruments. We have unusual measurement machinery -- RED-pin-first on every slice, pre-registered drills with hypotheses committed before data, seventeen structural checkers, independent cross-model review that refuses self-verification, a funnel that counts surfaced/useful/noise/helped. What we do NOT have is a destination. The 4.8pct funnel value rate is a number with no target: nobody can say whether 20pct would be good, or whether 4.8pct is fine for what we want. The n=5 kill-drill measured whether memory CAUSED a finding without a stated bar for how much would be enough to justify the machinery. Instruments without a win condition produce activity that cannot be scored as progress.

THE COMPARISON THAT MAKES IT CONCRETE: Max's own product (priori.sh) has a one-sentence success definition -- return only evidence that was knowable at a pinned instant -- and everything else in it serves that single testable claim: point-in-time versioning, BLAKE3 content hashes, sealed extraction locks, thirteen normalized sources, replay modes. The definition is what makes the feature list coherent rather than arbitrary.

CANDIDATE DEFINITIONS, and they are NOT compatible -- picking one changes what we build: (a) COLD-START COST -- a fresh seat reaches correct productive work in N minutes with zero re-explanation, measured as the fraction of a brief that re-carries standing premises; (b) DEFECT YIELD PER DOLLAR -- the fleet finds defects a solo agent does not, at a stated cost, which is what the kill-drill half-measures; (c) DECISION REPRODUCIBILITY -- any past decision can be replayed against what was knowable then, which is priori's axis and which our supersession model currently CANNOT do; (d) PORTFOLIO LEGIBILITY -- a hiring manager can read the artifact and see engineering judgement, which is Daniil's stated end goal and is measured by outside readers rather than by us. These pull in different directions: (a) optimises the boot fold, (b) optimises fan-out and review, (c) demands point-in-time query we have not built, (d) optimises for narrative and demonstration.

DANIIL DECIDES. This is not mine to pick -- it is the project's purpose, and picking it for him would be the T227 defect at the largest possible scale. What I can do is state the options with their consequences, and make each one's metric explicit so the choice is informed rather than abstract.

ACCEPTANCE: one stated success definition, in Daniil's words, recorded durably; at least one metric that operationalises it with a TARGET and not merely a current reading; a named thing we would STOP doing if it does not serve the definition -- because a definition that forbids nothing is a slogan; and the existing funnel/drill numbers re-expressed against the definition so we can say whether we are moving toward it.

BLOCKS T276, whose "where we stand versus the competition" section has no axis without this.

THE EYE: make the transcript plane queryable on multiple axes, built for the fleet to call. Daniil specified this on 2026-07-31 and it has never been built. His words, verbatim, recovered from session transcripts 2026-08-10: "I want you to be able to search redis and get a representation of the items referenced within. a realtime eye that you can quyery and understand your position and vision on multiple axees at once with ways of pinging and navigating quickly." And the constraint, same day: "I want the eye to have its own cursor, we cant have lookups breaking core system logic."

RESTATED 2026-08-10 after seeing priori.sh: "I want all of our transcripts to be quereable in useful ways with frequency, who was there, what is ambiant related knowledge. Make this be useful and useable for you." The last sentence is the design constraint: the CONSUMER IS THE FLEET, not a browsing human, so this is a door with structured output rather than a UI.

WHY IT KEEPS EVAPORATING, and this is the finding that makes it urgent: TWICE on 2026-08-10 a directive was lost because it lived only in session transcripts. The T276 research-cadence directive (2026-07-26, "we keep finding gold when we do this but we rarely do it") took four parallel repo searches that ALL came back empty, then three guessed substrings to recover. THE EYE ITSELF took another five. Both were quoted back later as standing policy and still never became organs. The transcript plane is the one input class the fleet cannot read, and it is where the founder actually speaks. The Eye is the fix for the exact failure that keeps burying the request for it.

FEASIBILITY VERIFIED, not assumed: 480 .jsonl transcripts, 440MB, at ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/. Schema carries type, timestamp, sessionId, uuid, parentUuid (threading), cwd, gitBranch, version, and message{role,content}.

THE TRAP, verified by reading records rather than trusting the type name: DANIIL'S SPEECH HIDES IN queue-operation RECORDS. A record with type=queue-operation and operation=enqueue carries a `content` field holding what he typed WHILE A TURN WAS RUNNING -- his mid-turn interjections, which he makes constantly (three times in the session that produced this task). Those are NOT type=user. An ingest reading only type=user silently drops every interruption he has ever made. The corpus already warned about this in learn:experiment:operator_speech_hides_in_queue_operation_records and I nearly built it wrong anyway.

THE AXES, his three plus what I actually needed today and did not have: (1) FREQUENCY -- how many times an idea appears, across how many sessions, on what dates. This is his sharpest contribution: a thing said ONCE is an idea, said THREE TIMES is a standing directive, and today the Eye scored 3x in a prioritization pass and still got dropped. Repetition is signal strength and nothing measures it. (2) WHO WAS THERE -- the seats live in that session, the model, the branch. (3) AMBIENT -- what else was in play at that timestamp: commits in the window, tasks touched, lessons filed, other utterances in the same session. (4) FULL UTTERANCE, not a 100-char snippet -- today I assembled ONE quote from four successive guessed substrings because the only available tool returns one snippet per session. (5) SURROUNDINGS via parentUuid, so "what was around it" is a traversal rather than a re-search. (6) AS-OF, so a past decision can be read against what was knowable then.

REFERENCE DESIGN, priori.sh (████████████'s product, seen 2026-08-10): its query surface is a TYPED FACET dropdown -- Source, Entity, Type, Relationship, Exact phrase -- with an as-of control beside it, and stable per-observation URLs. Exact phrase is the LAST facet, the fallback. That is the whole lesson: queryable means HAVING DIMENSIONS, not having embeddings. We already store five of those six dimensions (agent_id, task/file entities, atom and message types, replaces/related_to edges, bitemporal valid_from/valid_to) and expose exactly ONE of them -- the weakest, string matching. Embeddings are an ENHANCEMENT to a working facet surface, not a substitute for one; the socket is already specified in three modules (learning_store 'no embeddings, no LLM judge', event_query 'embedding relevance_fn is a later swap-in -- same 0..1 contract', codex/schema centroid field).

ACCEPTANCE, RED first: ingest captures BOTH type=user AND queue-operation/enqueue utterances, and a pin proves a known mid-turn interjection is present (the silent-drop case); a query returns the FULL utterance plus its session, timestamp, branch and neighbours, never a truncated snippet; frequency reports occurrence count ACROSS sessions with dates, so a 3x directive is distinguishable from a 1x aside; ambient returns what else happened in a stated time window; the Eye reads with ITS OWN CURSOR and a pin proves a lookup cannot advance or corrupt any live bus cursor -- Daniil's stated constraint, and the exact class we broke repeatedly this week with lane cursors; re-ingest is idempotent; and the whole thing answers "when did he first say X" in ONE call rather than five guesses.

A lesson is unreachable by any PREFIX of its own name, while every hook invites you to look it up by that name. Measured 2026-08-09, reproduction stable: recall backup_door_never_ran returns 4 hits with the lesson itself ranked FOURTH, below three lessons that merely mention it in prose; recall backup_door returns ZERO; recall cold_encounter returns ZERO while recall "cold encounter" with a space returns 32 hits including cold_encounter_test_measures_ergonomics.

CAUSE, read from source not inferred: learning_store.py around line 75, _TOKEN = [a-z0-9_]+ makes underscore part of a token, so a snake_case experiment_name is ONE ATOMIC SYMBOL. Whole-token matching then means a name matches only when typed in full and exactly.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: the system cites lessons BY THAT NAME everywhere. Every recall-at hook prints "source: learn:experiment:<name>" and the CLI tells the reader to run recall --full <source>. So the one identifier the system hands out is the one the search cannot partially match, and a half-remembered name -- the most natural way anyone reaches for a lesson -- returns silence rather than a near miss. It also lands on the resident arc directly: T261 catch-up packs cite lessons by name, and a resident asked why it is called what it is must type its receipt perfectly or get nothing.

THE ASYMMETRY WAS DELIBERATE, which is why this is a design question and not a typo. The module header records that splitting on underscore made the query gamma_lesson match the record alpha_lesson through the shared fragment "lesson" -- a real defect, really prevented. What was never measured is the COST of the cure: how often a partial-name query returns nothing that a fragment-split would have found. Both directions have a failure mode and only one was counted.

NOT A DUPLICATE: this was recorded as gap 3 inside T258's description, and T258 is DONE, so the defect currently has no live ledger entry. Also related but distinct from T273 (the clip chokepoint) and T278 (the Eye) -- this is the known defect in the ONE retrieval dimension we already expose, documented in the map atom art_20260810_retrieval-plane-inventory_647751.

ACCEPTANCE, RED first: a query that is a strict prefix of an existing lesson name finds that lesson; an EXACT full-name query ranks the record ITSELF first rather than fourth, since identity must outrank mention; the gamma_lesson/alpha_lesson cross-match the current design prevents STAYS prevented, pinned explicitly so the cure is not traded for the disease; and the fix is measured on both arms -- how many partial-name queries newly succeed, and how many spurious fragment matches appear -- because the original tradeoff was made without that number.

Query-grammar contract: ONE page specifying the read-door grammar every plane adopts -- as_of (known_at<=as_of law), facet params (who/kind/edge/task/file), degraded flag on clipped funnels, 422 on mis-shaped selectors (never silent-empty). T278 THE EYE is the first tenant, recall the second. Source: priori.sh live audit 2026-08-10 (lesson priorish_live_api_audit_corrects_screenshot_claims, artifact b4635845, sweep atom art_20260810). Grammar verified against a shipped product end-to-end through its MCP door.

tasks.title: read_file truncates BEFORE it slices, so every line past 120KB is silently unreachable while the door advertises the opposite. FOUND BY HEIMDALL under load, 2026-08-17: asked to independently verify T275 he could not read the ledger row he was judging and reconstructed it field-by-field through grep, then named the gap in his own report. MECHANISM (core/comm/toolbox.py read_file): raw=p.read_bytes(); text=raw[:MAX_FILE_BYTES].decode(); THEN if start_line/end_line: lines=text.splitlines(). The byte cap is applied to the INPUT, so the requested lines are cut off before the slice ever runs. Measured: MAX_FILE_BYTES=120,000; state/coord/tasks.json is 646,935 bytes; T275's row begins at byte offset 510,416 -- 4.25x past the cap. lines[10224:10240] indexes an array that ends near 2,000, so the call returns an EMPTY STRING. Not an error, not a truncation notice: silence. And the tool's own description reads 'Prefer start_line/end_line for big files to save tokens' -- it advertises precisely the capability it cannot deliver, which is the names-that-lie class at a door.
